product: MOLBREEVI (molgramostim inhalation solution), an inhaled recombinant human GM-CSF given through PARI's eFlow nebulizer for autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis. Phase 3 IMPALA-2 is complete; the BLA is under FDA Priority Review with MAAs under EMA review and MHRA accelerated review. Not approved anywhere.
demand: No revenue yet. Management cites Veeva claims data covering over 300 million lives that identified about 5,500 US autoimmune PAP patients, roughly 16 per million, plus over 1,000 confirmed direct-line-of-sight patients; 164 patients enrolled in IMPALA-2, 159 rolled into the open-label extension with 94% retention.
pricing_power: Management guides $400,000-$500,000 net per patient per year, with confidence in broad coverage and no material payer budget impact, citing no approved therapy, FDA Breakthrough Therapy and Priority Review designations, and formulation and device patents running to March 2041 and March 2043.
competition: No approved therapy exists in the US, EU or UK; management calls whole lung lavage the rescue-of-last-resort procedure. Sources read name no direct competitor. The 10-Q warns only generally about competition and notes a biosimilar could end the GEMA royalty early.
team: Chair and CEO Matt Pauls, Chief Commercial Officer Braden Parker, Executive Vice President Brian Robinson for medical affairs. Robert Lutz added CFO duties on Jul 15 2026 after David Lowrance resigned for health reasons with 12-month equity acceleration and $200 per hour consulting. Board re-elected Jun 4 2026.
market_strategy: US first as the nearest-term opportunity, then UK and EU. Commercial infrastructure is being built pre-approval: G&A rose 78.2% to $19.0M in Q2 2026 for headcount and commercial activity, 23 rare-disease specialists were hired, and non-promotional disease awareness precedes an early 2027 launch.
bull: FDA Priority Review with Nov 22 2026 PDUFA; EU/Australia formulation patents to 2041; ~$173M cash plus up to $150M non-dilutive if approved; ~5,500 US aPAP patients at $400k-$500k, no approved rival.
bear: FDA extended PDUFA three months on a major amendment with no CMC/safety reassurance; Fujifilm inspections pending; Q2 net loss widened to $40.2M; short interest 22.28% of float; Weiss reiterated Sell 2026-07-17.
falsifier: A Complete Response Letter for the molgramostim BLA on or before the 2026-11-22 PDUFA date, or FDA requiring a re-inspection of the Fujifilm drug-substance site before action.
web_what_changed: Jul 30 2026: EU and Australian liquid-formulation patents granted to March 2041. Aug 11 2026 Q2 results: BLA PDUFA Nov 22 2026, about $173M cash, up to about $150M non-dilutive capital if approved, UK MHRA decision Q4 2026, EMA Q1 2027. Aug 20 inducement grants; Aug 24 ERS presentations. Robert Lutz became CFO/COO Jul 15 2026.
web_not_known_yesterday: Not found. No primary filing or company release on Sep 24-25 2026; newest investor-relations item is Aug 24 2026 and EDGAR shows no 8-K since Jun 8 2026. Only aggregator coverage dated Sep 24 2026 (rttnews preview). Shares closed $5.07 on Sep 24 2026.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: No product revenue from inception per the 10-Q. Growth is a pre-launch volume build, not reported volume: management cites about 5,500 US aPAP patients, over 1,000 confirmed line-of-sight patients and a 23-person sales team. Price targeted at $400,000-$500,000 per patient per year; mix is not yet applicable with one asset.
web_suppliers: API from GEMABIOTECH SAU with a low-single-digit royalty and 10-year purchase requirement. Drug substance via Fujifilm Diosynth, about $57.1M accrued, with second-source tech transfer and FDA inspections still pending. PARI Pharma supplies the eFlow nebulizer, about $0.6M milestones. Single-source CMC previously triggered an FDA refuse-to-file.
web_customers: None. No product revenue and no named customers appear in filings. Future demand sits with about 5,500 US aPAP patients managed by pulmonologists, paid by US commercial plans and Medicare. Concentration is extreme by definition, so reimbursement and prior-authorization terms, not volume, drive early adoption.
web_who_loses: Whole lung lavage centers lose procedure volume, since management describes whole lung lavage as today's rescue-of-last-resort standard of care, and payers carry the new budget. No other named competitor was found in the sources read; treat off-label alternatives as unverified inference.
web_contradicting_evidence: FDA extended the PDUFA three months (announced April 2026) after deeming company responses a major amendment, with no safety, efficacy or CMC reassurance disclosed. An earlier refuse-to-file involved the first drug-substance supplier and Fujifilm inspections remain pending. Short interest is 22.28% of float, days to cover 36.25, up 4.63% month over month. Weiss Ratings reiterated Sell on 2026-07-17. Q2 net loss widened to $40.2M from $30.4M and G&A rose 78%.
web_if_management_right: FDA approves by Nov 22 2026, unlocking up to about $150M non-dilutive capital (RTW royalty plus Hercules debt) and a Q1 2027 US launch with 23 specialists; MHRA decides in Q4 2026 and EMA in Q1 2027; about 5,500 US patients at $400,000-$500,000 each drive a 2027 revenue ramp.
web_if_management_wrong: A November 2026 CRL breaks financing first: the approval-contingent $150M disappears, Hercules covenants bind (unrestricted cash from Apr 1 2027, revenue from Sep 30 2027), and about $173M cash against roughly $78M first-half burn forces a dilutive raise while the commercial build becomes stranded cost.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: PARI Pharma gains nebulizer sales and milestones, Fujifilm Diosynth gains commercial drug-substance work, GEMABIOTECH earns API royalties, RTW Investments and Hercules Capital earn royalty and debt returns, and rare-disease specialty pharmacies, distributors and labs testing LDH, KL-6 and CYFRA 21-1 gain volume.
